title: reduce-gpu-memory-and-workspace-optimizations-activation-checkpointing-arena-tuning-scratch-buffers
author: Ravi Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce peak GPU memory and transient workspace allocations for large generative models under the serving runtime. Customers on Dedicated and Private deployments hit OOMs with long sequences and mixed request patterns. This PR applies a set of coordinated runtime changes: 1) selective activation checkpointing policy to rematerialize only high-cost layers and preserve KV cache when possible, 2) arena/tuning changes to reduce per-allocation overhead and avoid fragmentation for scratch buffers, 3) pooled scratch buffers per CUDA stream with upper bounds to prevent runaway transient allocations, 4) kernel selection hints that prefer inplace/fused kernels which lower temporary workspace, and 5) scheduler tweaks for continuous batching to respect low-latency SLOs while enabling efficient packing that limits KV-cache growth per-batch. What changed (high level): - New selective activation checkpointing strategy in runtime/gpu/checkpointing.{h,cc}: calculable scoring per-layer based on activation size, FLOPs, and remat-cost. Default policy picks a small set of rematerialized layers to trade compute for ~30% peak memory reduction on long contexts. - Arena tuning: tuned default arena sizes (runtime/gpu/arena.cc) and added heuristics to grow arenas more conservatively. This reduces fragmentation and per-request scratch allocations for typical prompt-length distributions. - Scratch buffer pool: introduced a per-stream pooled scratch allocator (runtime/gpu/scratch_pool.cc) with caps and LRU reclamation for idle buffers. Avoids repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree at inference time and caps worst-case transient memory. - Kernel selection: added kernel hints and a new small fused attention kernel path (runtime/kernels/fused_attention.cc) that operates in-place for intermediate tensors, significantly reducing temporary workspace for medium sequence lengths. - KV cache compaction: compacted per-request KV pointers and introduced a per-batch compact-on-send pass that reclaims sparse holes when continuous batching merges multiple requests. - Scheduler/continuous batching: scheduler now tracks estimated KV-cache growth per-pending batch and prefers packing strategies that avoid unbounded KV growth; low-latency requests are still prioritized with an explicit fast-path. Testing and results: microbenchmarks run on p3.16xlarge (8xV100 equivalent) and A100 nodes. Representative results: average peak GPU memory reduced by 28-45% across the evaluated models (gpt-medium/gpt-large families) with typical sequence lengths 1k-8k. Median latency increase on cold paths: +3-6% (due to selective rematerialization) but tail latency improved because we avoid OOM-triggered retries/evictions. Continuous-batching throughput improved 5-12% because scratch reuse and compacted KV reduced memory pressure and allowed larger effective batch sizes. Compatibility and config: features are behind runtime flags and config knobs (see runtime/config/gpu_memory.yml). Defaults are conservative: selective checkpointing enabled for models > 6B, scratch pool enabled by default; arena tuning is opt-in via "arena.auto_tune: true" at install-time for Private. There is a Runtime API flag to opt-out per-model. Migration/rollout: Canary deployed to Dedicated capacity clusters for 48 hours with synthetic load and production shadowing. Monitors added: gpu.peak_memory, gpu.scratch_allocs, runtime.kv_cache_size, and a new alert when per-node transient allocation > 90% of node capacity. Release notes: see release_notes field. Short: improved GPU memory efficiency via selective activation checkpointing, arena tuning, pooled scratch buffers, and kernel workspace reductions. May increase CPU usage modestly due to rematerialization.
commits: feat(gpu): selective activation checkpointing policy and scoring function
perf(arena): conservative arena growth heuristics and defaults
feat(scratch): per-stream pooled scratch allocator with caps
feat(kernels): add small fused attention kernel that favors in-place ops
tests: add microbench harness for peak-memory and scratch reuse
docs: runtime config knobs and rollout playbook
review_comments: Lina Chen (2026-02-19): Could you add model-specific thresholds for when selective checkpointing should kick in? For smaller models the rematerialization cost isn't worth it.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-19): Added a config override to set per-model thresholds and included defaults based on #params and avg activation size.
Marco D'Souza (2026-02-20): The scratch_pool LRU eviction looks fine, but we should ensure it doesn't free buffers during a concurrent memcpy. Please add stream-synchronization asserts.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-20): Added synchronization guards and a stress test that ran 10k concurrent requests in the microbench harness.
Evan Brooks (2026-02-22): CI flagged a flaky integration test on scheduler packing logic. Please stabilize and document the nondeterminism window.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-23): Fixed packing nondeterminism by making heuristic deterministic for tests; added more unit tests to cover edge cases. CI green afterwards.
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory and transient workspace allocations via selective activation checkpointing, conservative arena sizing, pooled per-stream scratch buffers, and a fused in-place attention kernel. Default behavior is conservative and configurable. May trade modest CPU/rematerialization cost for significant memory savings. Recommended for Dedicated and Private deployments where OOMs are observed.
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator and checkpointing added. Microbench harness run on A100 and V100 nodes with synthetic traces and production shadowing during canary. Added integration tests to cover scheduler packing determinism. Monitors added to verify peak memory/per-node transient allocations during rollout.
